title: Hands-on SDKs Lab: Miniworkshop samples for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, and CLI (streaming & retries)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a compact, hands-on SDKs lab repository and a set of 4 minimal starter templates (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, CLI) that demonstrate: 1) idiomatic usage of Redwood Inference SDKs in Python/TypeScript/Go, 2) robust retry/backoff patterns for transient failures, 3) streaming ergonomics (resume, incremental rendering, error recovery), and 4) a cookbook page with short snippets and troubleshooting notes. Deliverables: - 4 starter apps with README + quickstart scripts - a single workshop guide (markdown) that instructors can run in 20 minutes - CI smoke tests for each template - docs PR with usage patterns and decision rationale
acceptance_criteria: Each template boots with a single command and authenticates using REDWOOD_API_KEY or local dev token
Retry/backoff examples included: exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency tokens for non-idempotent operations
Streaming example supports incremental render in Next.js (App Router streaming), FastAPI SSE endpoint, and Go HTTP chunked response; CLI shows retry+resume via local cursor
Code is in a dedicated samples/handson-lab folder in monorepo and has a README lab.md with timeboxed steps (<=20m)
Automated smoke CI runs: basic request + streaming + retry injection test for each template
Docs PR created and reviewed by SDK lead and DX writer with sign-off
notes: We should prioritize ergonomics for small teams onboarding to Redwood: minimal deps, clear patterns for when to prefer streaming vs polling, and a single place to look for retry knobs (timeouts, max attempts, jitter). Avoid heavy frameworks; prefer Next.js app-router example using native fetch and streaming transforms.
implementation_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/402: draft PR with Next.js and FastAPI examples
